bv.navHint: wheel zoom · Space / middle-drag to pan
bv.quiet.toggleHint: Click a number / probe mark to hide labels and frames; only a blinking inset pad outline remains. Click again to restore.
bv.quiet.activeHint: Quiet mode: inset pad dashes · click a mark or “Show marks” to restore
qc.empty: No parts on the board yet. Place parts in the schematic, sync to PCB and route, then come back for test flows.
qc.stage.preHint: After the fab board arrives, use a multimeter to verify net continuity and that supplies are not shorted before soldering.
qc.stage.postHint: After soldering: check shorts with power off, measure voltages with power on, then sample resistors and LEDs off-power.
qc.panel.flip: Move the step panel to the other side
qc.intro.jacksBody: : black probe always in COM; red probe in the VΩ jack (10A/20A jacks are for high current — not used here).
qc.intro.rangesBody: : 🔊 continuity — beeps when points connect; Ω resistance — pick a range above the value; V⎓ DC voltage — probes in parallel across the points.
qc.intro.safeBody: : power off for resistance / continuity; power on only for voltage. Touch metal pads or test points — don’t scrape the board.
qc.bar.note: Multimeter only this release; scope / electronic load come later
qc.bar.hint: {n} test flows · pick a step on the right to mark probe points
qc.step.plug: Black probe in COM, red probe in VΩ (not the high-current jack)
qc.ohm.auto: Auto-range, or start at 20kΩ and step up
qc.dial.beep: Continuity / beep (🔊; use diode range if missing)
qc.cont.title: Net {net} continuity
qc.cont.goal: Confirm copper for “{net}” runs from {a} to {b} with no open or etch defect.
qc.cont.s1: Touch the probe tips together first: you should hear a beep — meter and leads are OK
qc.cont.s2: Red tip on {ref} pad {num} (red highlight on the board)
qc.cont.s3: Black tip on {ref} pad {num} (black highlight on the board)
qc.cont.s4: Press lightly for solid contact; watch the reading and listen for the beep
qc.cont.fail: No beep or OL: the net is open. Trace the highlighted copper — possible fab defect (open / unplated hole).
qc.iso.title: {a} not shorted to {b}
qc.iso.goal: Confirm “{a}” and “{b}” copper are not connected — a short can destroy the supply or board at power-up.
qc.iso.s1: Red probe on {net} test point ({ref} pad {num})
qc.iso.s2: Black probe on {net} test point ({ref} pad {num})
qc.iso.s3: Hold 2–3 s and watch the reading
qc.iso.fail: Beep or near 0Ω: the nets are shorted. Check burrs, solder bridges, or design errors between the highlighted nets.
qc.short.title: {a} vs {b} impedance
qc.short.goal: After soldering and before power, confirm “{net}” is not shorted to ground by bridges or reversed parts.
qc.short.s1: Red on {a} ({aref} pad {anum}), black on {b} ({bref} pad {bnum})
qc.short.s2: Reading may climb as caps charge — wait until it settles
qc.short.expect: Usually hundreds of Ω or more when settled (a few kΩ with ICs is common); anything not near 0Ω is OK
qc.short.fail: Near 0Ω (< 10Ω): short present — do not power up. Check regulators and decoupling caps for bridges or reverse polarity.
qc.volt.title: {net} voltage
qc.volt.goal: With power applied, confirm “{net}” is at the right voltage so chips can run.
qc.volt.s0: Finish the short check above, then power the board (USB / battery)
qc.volt.fail: Much low or 0: check the regulator, fuse and solder joints; cut power if voltage looks wrong.
qc.res.title: {ref} ({value})
qc.res.goal: Confirm {ref} is soldered well and the value is correct.
qc.res.s0: Disconnect power; wait 10 s for caps to discharge
qc.res.s1: Probes on both pads of {ref} (red/black order does not matter)
qc.res.expectNom: About {v}; in-circuit readings are only lower, never higher
qc.res.expect: Near the marked value (in-circuit can read a bit low)
qc.res.fail: Much high or OL: cold joint / bad resistor; much low is often a parallel path — lift one end to check if unsure.
qc.led.title: {ref} ({value})
qc.led.goal: Confirm {ref} orientation and that the diode is good.
qc.led.s1: Red on {ref} pad {a}, black on pad {b}; note the reading
qc.led.expect: One way shows a drop (LED ~1.6–3V and may glow; silicon diode ~0.5–0.7V); the other way OL
qc.led.fail: OL both ways: cold joint or dead part; conducts both ways: shorted; vs silkscreen: reversed — rework.
asm.empty: No schematic-linked parts on the board. Place parts in the schematic and “Update PCB”, then return for assembly steps.
asm.orderHint: Industry order: small passives first, same value together; front SMD → back SMD → through-hole with an iron last. Paste → place → hot air / hot plate.
asm.detail.marks: Pads are numbered 1–{n} in assembly order — paste, place, then reflow together. Click a number for inset pad dashes only.
asm.tht.tool: Through-hole parts: solder from the back with an iron (~350°C); skip reflow.
asm.bar.title: Assembly · hand reflow
asm.bar.note: Front / back · 0/90/180/270° rotate · wheel zoom to match the real board
asm.bar.hint: Pick a step on the right; pads are numbered in order on the board
asm.hint.R: No polarity. Check the code (e.g. 103 = 10kΩ) — wrong value is the most common mistake.
asm.hint.C: MLCC has no polarity; electrolytic / tantalum do — dark stripe is usually negative (tantalum stripe is positive); reverse can explode.
asm.hint.D: Polarized! Match the cathode bar to the silkscreen; LED green mark / flat is usually cathode — diode-test if unsure.
asm.hint.L: No polarity. Small parts blow away easily — lower hot-air flow.
asm.hint.Q: Three-pin orientation is unique; align to the silkscreen outline.
asm.hint.U: Find pin 1: chip dot / notch to board silkscreen. Tack two opposite pins, check alignment, then solder the rest.
asm.hint.Y: Two-pin crystals have no polarity; four-pin oscillators mind pin 1. Avoid overheating — one reflow pass.
asm.hint.SW: Align pins with mounting holes; plastics hate heat — work quickly.
asm.hint.J: Mechanical parts need full fillet. USB / headers: tack one pin, square it, then finish.
asm.hint.other: Check BOM and silkscreen before soldering.
panel.syncHint: 回路図の完成後や変更後は、PCB を更新して部品とネット接続を同期してください。
